# UseArazzo

> A JavaScript/TypeScript toolkit for Arazzo, the OpenAPI Initiative's specification for multi-step API workflows. Validate documents, run workflows against live APIs, and read the trace of each step.

## What it does

1. Validate the document against the Arazzo specification.
2. Run the workflow against live APIs.
3. Read the trace of each step in run order: whether it succeeded, which action was selected, and how many attempts it took, alongside the workflow's outputs and final status.

The entire toolkit (CLI, Validator, Runner, plus the lower-level parser and resolver) is pre-1.0 and in heavy development. No package has been published to npm yet, and APIs may change without notice. Everything is built in the open in the arazzo-toolkit monorepo.

## Compatibility

| Document | Versions | Validate | Run |
| Workflow Document: Arazzo | 1.0.0, 1.0.1 | yes | yes |
| Workflow Document: Arazzo | 1.1.0 | no | partial |
| Source Description: OpenAPI | 2.0, 3.0.x, 3.1.x | yes | yes |
| Source Description: Arazzo | 1.0.0, 1.0.1 | yes | no |
| Source Description: AsyncAPI | any | no | no |

## Products

### CLI
- One command-line interface across the toolchain: validate and run workflows on your machine and in CI
- Not yet published to npm, in development
- Planned commands: `validate` (wraps @usearazzo/validator), `run` (wraps @usearazzo/runner)
- Under consideration, not built or decided: `init`, which would read a workflow and write an editable config file covering its inputs, the inputs of every dependsOn workflow (transitively), credentials from source-description security schemes, and server variables
- No cli package exists in the monorepo yet; the page is a design sketch, and feedback on it is welcome in Discussions
- Docs: {{ site.url }}{{ site.baseurl }}/cli/

### Validator
- Semantic validation and linting for Arazzo documents, with LSP-compatible diagnostics
- Opt-in JSON Schema (AJV) validation
- Supports Arazzo 1.0.0 and 1.0.1
- Pre-1.0, not yet published to npm, under heavy development
- Free, open source (Apache 2.0)
- Docs: {{ site.url }}{{ site.baseurl }}/validator/

### Runner
- Executes Arazzo workflows against live APIs described by OpenAPI source descriptions
- Step-by-step execution: criteria evaluation, output mapping, failure actions, retries, sub-workflows, dependsOn prerequisites, cancellation via AbortSignal
- Pluggable HTTP transport (a function from the built request to a WHATWG Response; global fetch by default)
- Credentials are applied by decorating the outgoing request with a requestInterceptor, not modelled in the Arazzo document, because Arazzo is auth-agnostic
- Server selection or override per call, with no silent fallback: a server matching nothing declared is never swapped for the first declared one
- Workflow-level successActions/failureActions replace a step's wholesale; workflow-level parameters merge, keyed by the (name, in) pair
- Pre-1.0, not yet published to npm, under heavy development in the open (as is every package in the toolkit)
- Supports Arazzo 1.0.0/1.0.1 workflows; OpenAPI 2.0/3.0.x/3.1.x source descriptions
- Free, open source (Apache 2.0)
- Docs: {{ site.url }}{{ site.baseurl }}/runner/

### Lower-level packages
- @usearazzo/parser: parses Arazzo documents into an ApiDOM data model
- @usearazzo/resolver: dereferences $ref/JSON Schema/components in Arazzo and OpenAPI documents
- Not yet published to npm, free, open source (Apache 2.0)

## Why UseArazzo

- Deterministic execution: a workflow that ran yesterday runs the same today
- The standard is the product: Arazzo implemented exactly as specified, with fixes contributed back to the specification instead of private extensions only our tools can read
- Portable artifacts: plain Arazzo documents in your repository, API workflows keep working even without the toolkit

## On the roadmap

None of these are built yet. They are planned, not shipping:

- Language Service: LSP-compatible library bringing Arazzo intelligence to any editor or tool (validation, completion, hover, go-to-definition, find references)
- Editor: browser-based editor for authoring and validating Arazzo workflows with real-time feedback
- VS Code Extension: Arazzo authoring inside VS Code, with real-time validation, semantic linting, autocompletion, live preview
- GitHub Actions: violations annotated on the diff, run trace rendered into the job summary, check status driven by step outcomes
- Agent Skills: task-shaped skills teaching agents to author, validate, fix, and debug Arazzo workflows
- MCP Server: generic Model Context Protocol server exposing validation and execution over any Arazzo document
- MCP Compiler: compiles a specific workflow into a dedicated MCP server, one typed tool per workflow
- Arazzo Transformers: explicit, versioned transformations for reshaping data between steps, declared as ordinary API calls

## Built on SpecLynx

UseArazzo is built end to end on SpecLynx (https://github.com/speclynx): the semantic parsing core, reference resolution, and standards discipline behind years of Swagger/OpenAPI tooling.
